overall: No Open Meeting Law violation: the Council could refer complaints to counsel after reviewing them at a meeting, and full-Council review satisfied the rule for complaints filed with committees.

allegations.summary: Council allegedly failed to review several OML complaints before voting to refer them to legal counsel to send responses on its behalf.
allegations.key_passage: Nothing in the regulations prevents a public body, once it has reviewed a complaint during a meeting, from delegating its response to an individual, such as legal counsel.

allegations.summary: Council allegedly reviewed OML complaints filed with its subcommittees, which the subcommittees themselves never reviewed.
allegations.key_passage: In this instance, where all of the members of the committees (specifically, the Committee on Public Works and Transportation and the Committee on Economic Development and Tourism) are also members of the full Council and were present for the meeting on July 12, that purpose was served when the full Council reviewed the complaints.
